parsed.explanation: Combined regime: the state is highly protective—anti-discrimination since 2008, full facilities access, hate-crime law since 2001, courts ordering care resumed, and a prison consent decree—but federal rules override it at entry, in federal facilities, and in federal custody. Visa officers must refuse cases with document/sex discrepancy and may consider permanent lifetime ineligibility for alleged misrepresentation; federal facilities are restricted by birth sex; federal custody has documented hormone denial/conversion practices and immigration-custody abuse. No imprisonment or execution for being trans is documented, and state remedies work, preventing a lower score.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal binary-sex order, X markers stopped for new US passports, Supreme Court allowed restrictions, and 2025 consular cable requires refusal where documents cast reasonable doubt on sex, with possible permanent fraud ineligibility. Foreign X/mismatched passports face this screening.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid until expiry; fraud finding requires four elements and is never automatic; state licences/birth certificates offer X and are changeable without surgery.
entry_documents.interaction: State document flexibility does not cancel federal visa/passport screening; a discrepancy at entry can become refusal or a fraud inquiry before state protections apply.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: From 2026 federal corrections adopted conversion-therapy model including hair cutting, hormone removal and psychiatric substitution; immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary and sexual abuse; DOJ reward system and counterterrorism strategy frame 'radical gender ideology/pro-transgender' groups for prioritisation.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: State prison class action produced 2024 consent decree: expanded healthcare, voluntary specialised housing, $2.1m compensation; separate $170,000 settlement.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: State consent decree mitigates state custody but does not govern federal prisons or immigration detention, where the documented harmful practices operate.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal order bars transgender people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity, creating birth-sex exposure in federal buildings despite state law.
federal_state_facilities.protection: State civil-rights ruling 2013, 2023 full bathroom access for all genders, anti-discrimination coverage of public accommodations.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State facilities protection is operative locally but does not pre-empt federal facility rules, federal buildings, or national agencies interacting with the traveller.

care_services.exposure: National orders target youth gender-affirming care, funding freeze, and a national rule blocking public funds; state public insurance for youth care suspended from 13 Oct 2026 requiring legislative action to restore.
care_services.protection: 2023 state law protects and guarantees safe passage for gender-affirming care; insurance must cover reassignment surgery; May 2026 state supreme court ordered hospital to resume blockers/hormones after suspension under national pressure.
care_services.interaction: State care protection works in court but national funding conditions directly suspend public coverage, limiting what the state can deliver to a minor traveller/resident.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Executive order defines sex as binary at birth, removes gender-ideology materials, bans 'gender/transgender/LGBT' terms in agencies, directs investigation/prosecution over teachers facilitating social transition, and federal counterterrorism prioritises 'radically pro-transgender' groups.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: State hate-crime law covers gender identity since 2001; 2009 first-degree murder hate-crime conviction; gay-panic defence abolished 2020; national hate-crime statute exists.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Federal threat-framing raises investigation/profiling risk nationally, while state prosecution history shows local courts will enforce bias-crime law when cases arise.

minors_guardians.exposure: National youth-care bans in 27 states, federal funding block, state suspension of public youth coverage Oct 2026, district bans on trans students in sex-aligned sports, and Nov 2026 ballot measures to ban trans children from gendered sports and childhood surgery.
minors_guardians.protection: State conversion-therapy ban for minors since 2019, redefined/expanded May 2026 with no limitations period; state court ordered resumption of youth care; 2023 safe-passage protection.
minors_guardians.interaction: Guardian travelling with a minor faces federal care/funding restrictions and possible state ballot restrictions despite state court protection; ballot outcome unresolved and not counted as law.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Not documented. No state-specific figure for killings/violence against transgender people versus general homicide rate appears in the dossier.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State hate-crime enhancements since 2001 and documented 2009 murder conviction with hate-crime finding; anti-bullying law covers gender identity.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Documented local enforcement signals police/court response may work for assault, but absence of a current violence rate means street-violence prevalence is not assessable from this dossier.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport-marker litigation, challenges to executive orders, and proposed health rules are unresolved; several orders enjoined; compliance with May 2026 hospital order, post-Oct 2026 document provisions, conversion-therapy challenge, and Dec 2025 sports settlement are not documented.
remedies_unknowns.protection: State courts have granted injunctions, consent decrees and damages; legal-aid FAQ on passport rules; national civil-liberties suit on behalf of seven plaintiffs.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are real in state courts but slow and contested federally, so a traveller cannot rely on timely relief at entry, in federal facilities, or in federal custody.

anchor_checks.comparison: Higher than 0.35: no routine visitor register, eviction, detention without charge or near-certain exclusion system. State courts and consent decree provide working remedies, and imprisonment/execution for trans status are not credible.

Similar to 0.55: extended secondary screening for document mismatch, discretionary refusal of admission, possible lifetime ineligibility inquiry, and facility placement by document marker. State protections are stronger, but federal entry/facilities exposure matches this tier.

Lower than 0.65: 0.65 involves brief hold then release with apology/compensation and no lasting bar. Here refusal can carry permanent-ineligibility consideration and federal custody/facility rules are operative, not merely inconsistent local practice.

Materially lower than 0.75: 0.75 has brief detention, counsel, written reasons and compensation. Here federal screening can refuse entry outright, federal facilities ban applies universally in federal buildings, and federal custody harm is documented.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller's journey moves from federal exposure to state protection and back to federal exposure. State law strongly protects daily life, facilities in state buildings, hate-crime recourse and care, with courts demonstrably ordering relief. It does not cancel federal visa screening, federal facilities, federal investigation framing, or federal prison/immigration custody practices. For a minor, national funding pressure already suspends state public youth coverage despite court-ordered care resumption. The operative risk is administrative refusal, forced outing, facility exclusion in federal settings, and severe harm only if federal detention occurs—hence Elevated/Reduced boundary at 0.55.
